correctness.rationale: An independent exhaustive edge-subset check used all 8-subsets of the 24 displayed edges, retaining just the 33 disjoint covers. For each pair of covers the symmetric difference is 2-regular on its support; the move test therefore requires cardinality 6 or 8 and one connected component. Floyd–Warshall then gave component sizes (1,1,1,30), (33), (33); distance counts by increasing positive distance (96,216,120,3), (36,198,54,240), (132,342,54); and eccentricity counts 24 at 3 and 6 at 4 in the nontrivial six-only component, 3 at 3 and 30 at 4 for eight-only, and all 33 at 3 for the union. The exact joint counts by complementary type and degrees agree with the claim, including three (8,8) types of degrees (0,12,12). Every octagon-only neighbor of a nonhub is a hub; each hub has eight leaves and there are exactly two length-two paths, via different degree-two states, for each hub pair. The base graph is bipartite by the displayed parts; counting simple 4-, 6- and 8-edge cycles gave 0,24,30, proving girth six and the connectivity cutoff of eight. The included permutation checker has a human-readable 'THREE_COMPONENTS' marker, but its assertion specifies four components (three isolates and one large component), which is what the independent check obtained.
residual_risks: The metric results refer to actual matchings, not orbit representatives or face-restricted moves. The radius and diameter of six-only trades are for its 30-state connected component.

value.rationale: This is a test case of bounded cycle exchanges where hexagons strand entire matching types, octagons already connect all matchings via an identifiable small core, and both together shorten the diameter and eliminate eccentricity differences. The exact state space and move geometry are useful beyond a recomputation of the known matching census.
